name: aa-deploy-runner
//: The AA console/deploy runner's OWN dependency tree. It is a separate process from the
kernel and does not share its lockfile, so this list is maintained here rather than
inherited. What MUST agree with the kernel pin
(effectstream/zswap-offerfiles-kernel @ 80bace37bc2412542452e1c597761b2ebce5c677,
branch ledger-v9, the Compact 0.34.0 head) is what crosses the wire between them:
@midnightntwrk/ledger-v9 1.0.0-rc.3 (the offer blob's ledger types),
@effectstream/mip-zswap-offer 0.4.0-v9.0 (the MIP-0005 encoding the kernel parses),
and @midnight-ntwrk/compact-runtime 0.19.0 next to compactc 0.34.0, which is the
version the pinned kernel tree declares in infra/compact-version.txt and which the
image reads from there rather than hard-coding.
0.19.0, NOT 0.18.0-rc.1, since 00015: this process loads BOTH generated contract
modules and each opens with checkRuntimeVersion(<what compactc emitted>). compactc
0.34.0 emits 0.19.0, so 0.18.0-rc.1 would refuse to load the contracts at the first
console action. The image now PROVES the agreement instead of asserting it in prose:
the compact stage compares compactc --runtime-version against the kernel's contract
package, and the runtime stage compares it against what bun install resolved here,
requiring exactly one copy. That pair of checks is what closed infra issue 00011.
AA_REF 41de69d is itself a 0.34.0 build (AA PR #11), so both contract sets are now
compiled by the compiler their authors used, rather than relying on the measured
0.33/0.34 ZKIR equality that made the previous pin combination safe.
The MinoCrab release supplies execute's ZKIR and keys instead of that
build (see the image Dockerfile) but adds NO dependency here: it is data, not code.
@effectstream/midnight-contracts and @effectstream/utils stay at 0.200.1 here while the
kernel resolves 0.200.2: they are used for this process's own network config and
contract helpers, never for anything the kernel deserializes.
The override collapses ledger-v9 to ONE wasm copy — two copies in one process fail
instanceof checks (the documented trap).
//overrides: ledger-v9 collapses to ONE wasm copy: two copies in one process carry different
per-instance class identity and every cross-copy value fails an instanceof check.
compact-runtime is pinned for the adjacent reason, and it became NECESSARY with
and @effectstream/midnight-contracts each declare an EXACT 0.18.0-rc.1, so without this
override bun installs FOUR copies — the hoisted 0.19.0 plus three nested 0.18.0-rc.1 —
MEASURED in the image build on 2026-09-04, which is what the runtime stage's
one-copy assertion caught. The generated contract modules resolve upward to the hoisted
0.19.0 and load, but two runtimes around one onchain-runtime-v4 wasm is the same trap
the ledger-v9 pin above exists to avoid. The pinned kernel makes exactly this override
at its own root (PR #67) and gates it with scripts/check-compact-runtime.ts.
